dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows pictures small on its pages — a photograph in an article, the pictures of a thing for sale, an attachment in a conversation, a screenshot in a guide — and lets a person look at one closely: over the page, enlarged and moved about, and on to the next picture of the set without going back.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything an image preview draws itself: the surface that fills the window; the bar at the top (its least height, fill, inset, the gap between its controls and which Button variant they take); the count; which Button variant the previous and next controls take and how far they stand from the edges; the caption (fill, text style, color, padding, widest line); the gap between two pictures while one replaces the other; the mark and the sentence of a picture that did not arrive; and the motion of opening, closing, a zoom step, a move to another picture and the controls' fade. Its controls are Tanrei Buttons and its loading placeholder a Skeleton: their looks are comp.button.* and comp.skeleton.*, never repeated here.
rules: The preview is opened by the product: set open and index from the product's own thumbnail, which is a button that says it enlarges the picture. Every picture has an alt; a caption is optional.

Never hide a way out: the close button, the previous and next buttons and the zoom buttons are always in the focus order and exposed to assistive technology, drawn or not. Every gesture has a button and a key.

The surface is the theme's own surface in both themes. A product that wants its pictures on a dark stage in both themes re-values container.color, bar.container.color and caption.container.color with the count, caption and error colors in its layer — the pairs must keep their contrast.
Change how the controls stand out by re-valuing bar.button.variant and navigation.button.variant; never restyle a Button from here.
It shows still pictures. A video, a document or a map is the product's own view.

color.$description: The surface that fills the window behind the picture, and what shows through a picture's transparent parts. The theme's own surface in the light and in the dark theme: the preview is a view of the product like any other, not a room of another color.

height.$description: The least height of the bar at the top; it grows where the count wraps. The picture at fit ends below it (IMP-11).

color.$description: The fill of the bar, over a zoomed picture that passes under it.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product lets an enlarged picture show through its bar by giving the bar a fill that is partly clear; another keeps the bar solid so that its controls never stand on a picture.

padding-inline.$description: Between the bar's first and last control and the window's safe area at each side.

gap.$description: Between two controls of the bar. With the small Buttons' own targets (BTN-5) it keeps each whole pointer target apart from the next in the default system: 32 and 12 make sys.target.pointer's 44.

variant.$description: The Button variant of the bar's controls — zoom out, zoom in and close — icon-only small Buttons (IMP-8): tonal in the default system, as every host's close button is, and the zoom controls beside it drawn the same way. The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values, the core Button variants; platforms receive the name.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product decides once how the controls of its previews stand out: tonal controls that read as controls on any bar, bare glyphs on a solid bar, or filled controls on a bar that lets the picture through.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A choice of kind; no dial scales it.

typescale.$description: The count's text style: a short line of interface text, as a label is.

color.$description: The count: secondary to the picture and to the controls.

padding-inline.$description: Before and after the count, so that its text begins where the caption's padding begins.

variant.$description: The Button variant of the previous and next controls, icon-only medium Buttons that stand over the picture's sides (IMP-10). The value is an index into dev.tanrei.enum.values, the core Button variants; platforms receive the name.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product's previous and next controls stand on whatever the picture shows, so it chooses a variant with a fill of its own; which fill is the product's.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A choice of kind; no dial scales it.

margin-inline.$description: Between the previous or the next control and the window's safe area at its side.

color.$description: The fill behind the caption, over a zoomed picture that passes under it.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: The caption's fill is set apart from the bar's because one product keeps its captions readable on a solid fill while its bar lets the picture through.

typescale.$description: The caption: a sentence about the picture, read at the interface's reading size.

color.$description: The caption's color: here the caption is the text of the view, not small print under a frame.

padding-block.$description: Above and below the caption's text.

padding-inline.$description: Before and after the caption's text, inside the window's safe area.

max-width.$description: The widest the caption's column draws, centred in the window; its lines begin at the column's start.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product opens the same preview on a phone and on a wide display, and a sentence set across a wide display is not read.

page-gap.$description: Between the picture that leaves and the one that arrives while one replaces the other, so that two pictures with the same edge color do not read as one.

size.$description: The mark of a picture that did not arrive.

color.$description: The mark's color: a quiet statement, not the error status — nothing the person did failed and nothing is theirs to correct.

typescale.$description: The product's sentence under the mark.

color.$description: The sentence's color, as the mark's.

gap.$description: Between the mark and the sentence.

zoom-duration.$description: A zoom step by a button, a key or a double tap, and the return to fit. A pinch follows the fingers and has no duration.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product tunes how quickly a picture answers a zoom step apart from how its overlays open: slow enough to follow the point that was tapped.

page-duration.$description: The move to another picture by a button or a key, and the settle of a released drag.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product tunes how a set of pictures turns, apart from a zoom and from an overlay's entrance.

controls-duration.$description: The fade of the bar, the previous and next controls and the caption when they are hidden or shown.
